MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 12, 2018

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Sachs at 5:00 p.m., on June 12, 2018, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on June 7, 2018, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Goodell
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Sachs

Absent:  Council Member Kelley

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

 CS1.  Conference with Legal Counsel – Anticipated Litigation: Significant Exposure to
  Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph (2) or (3) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 –
  Threat of Litigation From City of Santa Ana to Compel Homeless Management,
  Support or Housing

 CS2.  Conference with legal Counsel: Anticipated Litigation Initiation of Litigation
  Pursuant to Paragraph 4 of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 (1 case)

 CS3.  Conference with Legal Counsel – Existing Litigation (Paragraph (1) of subdivision
  (d) of Section 54956.9): City of Mission Viejo v. State of California, DOF

City Council Minutes  1  June 12, 2018
  CS4.  Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of
  City Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Sachs recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:03 p.m. with four City Council Members present (Council Member Kelley was
absent).

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there were four matters addressed in Closed Session.
The City Council provided direction to staff but there was no reportable action.

INVOCATION: Mayor Sachs

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Goodell

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Jason Yi, M.V.: announced that the Community of Character Committee raised over $1,300 in last
weekend’s Relay for Life. He discussed traits that demonstrate this month’s character word which
is citizenship and announced that the character film for the month of June will be John Adams,
shown in the Council Chamber on June 24, 2018, at 2:00 p.m.

Chris Yellin, M.V.: speaking on behalf of the Nadadores Foundation and its Board Members, she
expressed the Nadadores unwavering gratitude for the City’s collaboration on what is continuing
to be a landmark in Mission Viejo - the Marguerite Aquatics Center. To express their thanks, Mrs.
Yellin, and the other Board Members present, gave the City the sign that hung on the former dive
tower for 40 years.

Steve Rhorer, M.V.: stated that he has been a member of Montanoso Recreation Center since 1996
and he recently joined a spin class there. He said he was disappointed to learn that the class will
be canceled due to funding and he asked the City Council to look at ways to continue the spin
classes.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to approve
the Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Kelley
City Council Minutes  2  June 12, 2018
 1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of May 22, 2018, as presented.

2.  Check Register Dated May 11, 2018 in the Amount of $1,076,828.16

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register dated May 18, 2018 in the amount of $2,088,219.91

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register dated May 25, 2018 in the amount of $867,084.56

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Community Development  Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for April 2018

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for April

  Received and filed.

  Received and filed.

9.  2018 Fourth of July Community Street Faire

  Approved the Special Events Permit submitted by the Mission Viejo Activities Committee

10.  First Amendment to Agreement with Consultant SWA Group for Oso Creek
  Revitalization Professional Services.

City Council Minutes  3  June 12, 2018
   Approved First Amendment to Agreement with SWA Group for an additional $30,000
  resulting in a total not-to-exceed amount of $98,000 for Oso Creek Revitalization
  Professional Services.

11.  Easement Deeds with Lake Mission Viejo for Landscape Maintenance

  Approved the Maintenance Easement Deed and authorized the City Manager to execute
  the Deed for Lake Mission Viejo Parcels located along the “Lake Loop” of the Oso Creek

12.  Extraordinary Tree Trimming and Brush Removal for Fuel Reduction- West Coast
  Arborists, Inc.

  (1) Approved the Twenty-Third Amendment with West Coast Arborists, Inc. in an amount

  Year Operating Budget by $80,000.00.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

NEW BUSINESS

13.  Banking Services

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, (1) for
  the City Council to approve of the selection of U.S. Bank to provide banking service to the
  City of Mission Viejo for the two-year period July 1, 2018, through June 30, 2020, and
  authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement; (2) for the Mission Viejo Housing
  Authority Board to approve the selection of U.S. Bank to provide banking services to the
  Mission Viejo Housing Authority for the two-year period July 1, 2018, through June 30,
  2020, and authorize the Executive Director to execute the agreement; and (3) for the
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency of the City of Mission Viejo
  Board to approve the selection of U.S. Bank to provide banking services to the Successor
  Agency of the Community Development Agency for the two-year period July 1, ,through
  June 30, 2020, and authorize staff to execute the agreement.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Kelley

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, (1)
  adopt Resolution 18-20 Amending Council Policies pertaining to Claims Against the City;
  Management and Budget Policies; and (2) approve the Debt Management Policy and

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  Administrative Services Manager Susan Knudson outlined the staff report and Director of

STAFF REPORTS

21.  Joint OCSD and OCFA Report on Homeless Issues

  Lt. Vuong and Chief Capobianco presented the report on homeless issues and fire
  prevention efforts.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

19.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Sachs presented the report.

20.  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Council Member Bucknum presented the report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

22.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

City Council Minutes  6  June 12, 2018
 City Council Minutes  7  June 12, 2018
 Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum announced a fundraising event called Boots, Beer and Barbecue on
July 22, 2018, at the Murray Community Center from 4:00 to 7:00 p.m. The fundraiser will benefit
the Mission Viejo Foundation and the Marines and Sailors Adoption Committee. Food will be
provided by Outback Steakhouse and there will be music and line dancing, among other activities.
Tickets are $25 and can be purchased at the Norman P. Murray Community Center front desk.
Council Member Bucknum announced that she had the opportunity to attend Coffee with a Cop
this morning. She said it was very well attended and she thanked the Sheriff’s Department team
for hosting it. She noted that some residents asked if the next Coffee with a Cop could be held on
a Saturday and Lieutenant Vuong responded that the next event will be an ice cream social. Council
Member Bucknum outlined her attendance at the Community of Character Youth Committee gala
and she encouraged young people to get engaged with the program at their school by joining or
establishing a character group. She also attended the Mission Viejo Film Festival, the Orange
County Triathlon, and the Capistrano Valley High School (CVHS) graduation and 40th year
celebration. Council Member Bucknum reminded residents that Mission Viejo High School and
Trabuco Hills High School will hold their graduation ceremonies this week and to be cognizant of
related traffic issues. She thanked staff for a great South County Relay for Life event which raised
almost $200,000 and she also thanked the Rotary Club for their involvement. For those interested,
she said donations can be made through the month of August.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell discussed the Orange County Triathlon and said he heard many positive
comments about the great course and the participants thanked the City for making it available. He
also thanked the Lake Mission Viejo Association and the sponsors of the event for making it such
a success. The triathlon sold out with 650 racers this year and Council Member Goodell said he
was able to participate by giving out the awards. He reminded residents of the Nadadores 50 year
reunion, which will start with a Friday night cocktail reception on June 15 at 5:00 p.m. at the
Murray Community Center, and on Saturday, June 16 there will be events at the Marguerite
Aquatics Complex and the lake. He said he hopes that anyone and everyone who ever had
something to do with the Nadadores team will come out and celebrate with old friends.
Commenting on the Economic Development Committee, Council Member Goodell said the City
put out a request for proposals for Site C, which is one of the designated affordable housing
locations. Staff received three proposals and they are working through questions and clarifications
at the present time. Council Member Goodell said there are elements in some of the proposals that
could qualify for low income supportive housing and the Economic Development Committee will
come back to the Council when the proposals are ready. He said the Committee is also interested
in further developing the civic core project.

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Mayor Pro Tem Raths noted that resident Rudy Padrol had to leave meeting early but wanted to
announce that this year’s Relay for Life event raised $182,000 of the $200,000 goal. He said the
Mission Viejo Rotary Club was out in full force and Commissioner Dave Leckness hosted the
“Fastest Kid in Town” race and everyone had a great time. There will be another Relay for Life
opportunity at Angels Stadium on June 23 and additional information is available on Rudy Padrol’s
City Council Minutes  8  June 12, 2018
 Facebook page. Mayor Pro Tem Raths announced that Second Harvest Food Bank of Orange
County is bringing a free mobile walk-up market to the Murray Community Center each week to
deliver food to seniors. Participants must first complete an intake form then they can come out
every Friday to pick up their food. Mayor Pro Tem Raths outlined recent events including the
Memorial Day ceremony, the Mission Viejo Film Festival, and the Cordova Park grand opening.
In closing, he announced that he has just completed ethics training for his service on the Orange
County Veterans Advisory Council.

Mayor Sachs

Mayor Sachs announced that he was pleased to kick off the Relay for Life event with
representatives from Lake Forest and Rancho Santa Margarita. This was the first South County
regional event and it was very well attended. He said he also enjoyed the Cordova Park opening
and although some residents are expressing concern about shade, he encouraged folks to give the
trees a chance to grow. Mayor Sachs announced that he is excited that the MV Shuttle continues
to grow and that the route is going north. The shuttle will now include stops at Casta del Sol which,
he said, will increase ridership. It will also go to Lake Mission Viejo among other new destinations.
Mayor Sachs stated that he is so grateful to be part of Mission Viejo. Two weeks ago, the Council
listened to residents who were fearful about what was going on around their homes and potential
fire dangers. He couldn’t believe how quickly City staff and public safety personnel started
mitigating the brush and he said it is apparent that they work very hard to make this a comfortable
and safe place for people to live and raise their families. Mayor Sachs thanked staff for digging in
and the Sheriff's deputies and the firefighters for their tireless efforts. He encouraged residents to
thank a firefighter or police officer whenever they see one.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:10 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Sachs adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, June 26, 2018, at 5:00 p.m.
